sections.reason: Title block, Status of This Memo, Copyright Notice, Abstract and Table of Contents. The Abstract restates the Introduction and directs no speaker.

Introduction. Indicative prose: correlating a session teardown with an offline notice is troublesome, and this document updates RFC 4486 by specifying a mechanism to carry a short freeform UTF-8 message in a Cease NOTIFICATION. It states what the document does, never what a speaker must do.

Requirements Language. The BCP 14 key-words paragraph, which also states that the key words bind only when they appear in all capitals. It tells a reader how to read the other sections and binds no speaker, which is why the derivation excludes it from the site inventory.

Shutdown Communication. The document's whole normative surface for the wire format: four capitalised MUST-level sites, mapped below to RFC8203-2-1 through RFC8203-2-4. Its remaining directives are the opening MAY (a speaker MAY include a UTF-8 string) and the closing SHOULD (reporting mechanisms SHOULD include methods such as Syslog); both are the unsourced ids below. Three sentences the site scan cannot see are descriptive, not obligations: the Figure 1 field diagram and its Error Code 6, the note that a multibyte Shutdown Communication holds fewer characters than the length value, and "This field is not NUL terminated", which describes the field rather than directing a receiver. Ze's receiver already reads exactly the length-prefixed extent and never scans for a terminator (Notification.ShutdownMessage, internal/component/bgp/message/notification.go).

Operational Considerations. Encourages operators to describe the reason for the shutdown and works through the "[TICKET-1-1438367390] software upgrade" example. Advice to an operator writing a message, with no RFC 2119 keyword and no directive to an implementation.

Error Handling. Two directives, neither MUST-level and neither visible to the site scan: an invalid Length value or an invalid UTF-8 sequence SHOULD be logged for the attention of the operator, and the malformed Shutdown Communication MAY be logged in a hexdump format. Both are the unsourced ids below.
IANA Considerations. Records that IANA references this document, in addition to RFC 4486, for subcodes 2 and 4 in the "Cease NOTIFICATION message subcodes" registry. Binds IANA, not a speaker.

Security Considerations. Carries one capitalised site, the REQUIRED UTF-8 "Shortest Form" encoding, mapped below to RFC8203-6-1. This is the ONLY place RFC 8203 states shortest form; its section 2 does not, which is a real difference from RFC 9003, where the same sentence appears in both sections. The rest is risk narration: the Unicode issues of UTR36, the syslog-injection risk the 128-octet limit is said to limit, forgery and snooping without an integrity or confidentiality transport, and the RFC 6973 data-minimization advice. Each is stated as advice to implementers and operators, with no keyword.
References. Section header for the two reference lists below.
Normative References: RFC 2119, RFC 3629, RFC 4271, RFC 4486, RFC 8174.
Informative References: RFC 4272, RFC 5424, RFC 6973, UTR36.

sites.quote: Subcode: the Error Subcode value MUST be one of the following values: 2 ("Administrative Shutdown") or 4 ("Administrative Reset").
sites.reason: The sender's subcode constraint, captured verbatim as RFC8203-2-1 at [MUST]. Ze's receiver enforces the same pair from the other side: Notification.ShutdownMessage returns an empty string for any Cease subcode other than NotifyCeaseAdminShutdown or NotifyCeaseAdminReset (internal/component/bgp/message/notification.go).

sites.quote: The length value MUST range from 0 to 128 inclusive.
sites.reason: The 0-to-128 length bound, captured verbatim as RFC8203-2-2 at [MUST]. This is the sentence RFC 9003 DELETES, so the obligation is owned by RFC 8203 alone and has no RFC 9003 counterpart at MUST level. Ze's sender holds it: MaxShutdownMessageLen is 128 and BuildShutdownData truncates a longer message back to a UTF-8 character boundary (notification.go).

sites.quote: Shutdown Communication: to support international characters, the Shutdown Communication field MUST be encoded using UTF-8.
sites.reason: The UTF-8 encoding obligation on the Shutdown Communication field, captured verbatim as RFC8203-2-3 at [MUST].

sites.quote: A receiving BGP speaker MUST NOT interpret invalid UTF-8 sequences.
sites.reason: The receiver's prohibition on interpreting invalid UTF-8, captured verbatim as RFC8203-2-4 at [MUST NOT]. ShutdownMessage returns errShutdownMessageContainsInvalidUtf8 and an empty string rather than the decoded bytes, so nothing invalid reaches an interpreter.

sites.quote: UTF-8 "Shortest Form" encoding is REQUIRED to guard against the technical issues outlined in [UTR36].
sites.reason: The REQUIRED UTF-8 "Shortest Form" encoding, captured verbatim as RFC8203-6-1 at [MUST] and read from section 6, which is the only section of RFC 8203 that states it.
